'''''Porphyra umbilicalis''''', commonly known as '''laver''', is a species of seaweed in the genus ''[[Porphyra]]''. It is smooth in texture and forms delicate, sheetlike [[thallus|thalli]], reaching {{Convert|25|cm|frac=2}} long<ref name="tfb">{{Cite book |last=Francis-Baker |first=Tiffany |title=Concise Foraging Guide |date=2021 |publisher=[[Bloomsbury Publishing|Bloomsbury]] |isbn=978-1-4729-8474-6 |series=[[The Wildlife Trusts]] |location=London |pages=201}}</ref> and often clinging to rocks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=''Porphyra umbilicalis'' Kützing 1843 |url=http://www.algaebase.org/search/species/detail/?species_id=102 |access-date=2008-08-10 |publisher=www.algaebase.org}}</ref> ''Porphyra'' is classified as [[red algae]]; it tends to be a brownish colour, but boils down to a dark green pulp when prepared. It is unusual amongst seaweeds because the fronds are only one cell thick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=laverbread – WalesOnline |url=http://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/wales-news/tm_objectid=14828141&method=full&siteid=50082&headline=laverbread-name_page.html |access-date=2008-08-10 |publisher=www.walesonline.co.uk}}</ref><ref>[http://www.nmbaqcs.org/downloads/macroalgae/EA%20Seaweed%20reference%20manual.pdf Wells, Emma (2010), ''A Field Guide to the British Seaweeds'', National Marine Biological Analytical Quality Control Scheme (p 24)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327191056/http://www.nmbaqcs.org/downloads/macroalgae/EA%20Seaweed%20reference%20manual.pdf |date=2012-03-27 }}.</ref><!-- At least Monostroma is also one cell thick, and the walls of Enteromorpha tubes are too. -->

It is commonly found around the west coast of [[Great Britain]] and east coast of [[Ireland]] along the [[Irish Sea]], where it is also known as "{{lang|ga|sleabhac}}{{-"}} or "slake".<ref>{{Cite web |title=British food seaweeds |url=http://everything2.com/title/British+food+seaweeds |access-date=6 May 2012 |publisher=[[Everything2]]}}</ref><ref name="eatweeds">{{Cite web |title=Laver Seaweed – A Foraging Guide to Its Food, Medicine and Other Uses |url=https://www.eatweeds.co.uk/laver-porphyra |access-date=22 March 2021 |website=eatweeds.co.uk}}</ref> It is [[edible seaweed|edible]] and used to make [[laverbread]].<ref name="tfb" /> In some parts of the [[United Kingdom]] it is classified as critically endangered following steep decline of its population in previously established habitats.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brodie |first=Juliet |last2=Wilbraham |first2=Joanna |last3=Maggs |first3=Christine A. |last4=Baldock |first4=Lin |last5=Bunker |first5=Francis |last6=Mieszkowska |first6=Nova |last7=Scanlan |first7=Clare |last8=Tittley |first8=Ian |last9=Wilkinson |first9=Martin |last10=Yesson |first10=Chris |date=2023-10-01 |doi-access=free|title=Red List for British seaweeds: evaluating the IUCN methodology for non-standard marine organisms |journal=Biodiversity and Conservation |language=en |volume=32 |issue=12 |pages=3825–3843 |doi=10.1007/s10531-023-02649-0 |issn=1572-9710}}</ref>
